한국이 새로운 길을 발견했다면, 영국은 그 길의 경제성을 계산하기 시작했다. 이유는 간단하다. 영국은 북극항로를 통해 들어오는 화물을 받는 도착 시장이기 때문이다. 누가 먼저 항로를 열었는지보다 중요한 것은 화물이 얼마나 빨리, 저렴하게, 안정적으로 도착하느냐다.  영국에도 북극항로가 가져올 이익은 분명하다. 가장 직접적인 효과는 동북아시아에서 생산된 상품을 더 빠르게 공급받을 수 있다는 것. 특히 세계 최고 수준의 우리 기술로 만든 자동차 부품과 배터리, 전자제품, 화학제품과 소비재가 기존보다 빨리 들여올 수 있다면, 수입 기업은 재고와 운전자본 부담을 줄일 수 있다.  영국의 소매업체에도 새로운 선택지가 될 수 있다. 계절성 상품이나 신제품처럼 판매 시기를 놓치면 가치가 크게 떨어지는 제품은 항공운송을 이용하면 빠르지만 비용이 높다. 반대로 기존 해상운송은 저렴하지만 시간이 오래 걸린다. 북극항로가 안정적으로 운영된다면, 항공보다 저렴하면서 기존 해상운송보다 빠른 중간 선택지가 된다. 공급망 안정성 측면에서도 마찬가지다. 수에즈운하와 홍해에서 문제가 발생할 때, 북극항로는 영국 기업이 선택할 수 있는 대체 경로가 될 수 있다. 다시 말하지만, 공급망에서는 최저 비용의 경로 하나보다 위기에 작동할 수 있는 대안 하나가 더 큰 전략적 가치를 지닌다.  영국의 펠릭스토우항 역시 부산항과 마찬가지로 직접적인 수혜자가 될 것이다. 이 항만이 북극항로의 영국 관문으로 자리 잡으면 신규 선박과 화물을 유치하고, 하역, 통관, 내륙 운송 수요도 함께 늘어난다. 컨테이너는 펠릭스토우항에 도착한 뒤 철도와 트럭을 통해 런던을 비롯한 영국 전역으로 이동한다. 항만의 물동량 증가는 주변 창고와 운송회사, 철도 화물, 물류 서비스 산업의 성장으로 이어진다.  그러나 영국의 계산은 지금부터다. 영국으로 들어오는 화물이 충분하더라도, 귀항 선박을 채울 물량을 확보하지 못한다면 왕복 운항의 수익성은 떨어진다. 며칠 빠른 도착이 매력적이더라도, 돌아가는 배가 빈 상태라면 실제 이용으로 이어지기 어렵다.  운항 예측 가능성도 핵심이다. 북극항로는 해빙과 기상의 영향을 크게 받는다. 빠르게 도착하는 것보다 정해진 시기에 비슷한 일정으로 반복 운항할 수 있어야 한다. 도착일을 예측하기 어렵고 위험관리가 복잡하다면, 생산 계획과 판매 일정을 맞추기 힘들다. 영국이 원하는 것은 '가장 빠른 항해'가 아니라 '예측 가능한 서비스'다.  러시아와의 관계도 외면하기 어렵다. 북극항로를 이용하면 홍해와 중동의 지정학적 위험은 피할 수 있지만, 러시아의 항행 허가와 해빙 정보, 구조 및 쇄빙 지원에 대한 의존이 커진다. 로이터는 한국의 첫 북극항로 운항이 서방의 대러시아 고립 정책과 마찰을 빚을 수 있다는 점을 짚었다.  이는 북극항로의 역설을 보여준다. 한국과 영국은 홍해 분쟁, 중동 불안, 수에즈 운하 병목을 피할 수 있지만, 그 결과 러시아가 실질적으로 영향력을 행사하는 해역과 서비스에 새롭게 의존할 가능성이 생긴다. 하나의 지정학적 위험을 피해 다른 지정학적 위험으로 들어갈 수 있다는 뜻이다.  환경적 비용도 계산에 넣어야 한다. 항해 거리가 줄어들면 전체 연료 사용량과 이산화탄소 배출량이 감소할 가능성은 있다. 그러나 선박에서 나오는 블랙카본, 그을음 입자는 눈과 얼음 위에 쌓여 햇빛 반사를 줄이고 열 흡수를 높인다. 이는 해빙을 더 빠르게 하고 북극 온난화를 가속할 수 있다.  사고 발생 시, 위험도 크다. 이곳에서 기름 유출 사고가 발생하면 차가운 해수 탓에 기름 분해가 느리고, 유출유가 얼음 사이에 갇힐 경우 제거 작업이 복잡해진다. 사고 해역까지 구조선과 인력이 도착하는 데 오랜 시간이 걸린다는 점도 문제다. 따라서 거리 단축만으로 북극항로를 친환경적인 운송로라고 부르기는 어렵다.  ddanzi.com/ddanziNews/894472… #딴지 #북극항로 #한국 #영국 #러시아

Nightmare-Eclipse drops ShieldCrash, a third-generation Windows Defender privilege-escalation PoC that survived both Microsoft's July and September 2026 patches. The same object-manager abuse mechanism has now outlasted two remediation rounds.  - ShieldCrash is the follow-on to ShieldBreak (CVE-2026-69414, patched September 2026), which itself bypassed RoguePlanet (patched July 2026). All three exploit the same object-manager mount-and-symlink path into Defender's shadow scanning subsystem. The actor released it as a deliberate skeleton: LevelBlue testing confirmed it returns ntdll.dll regardless of target, not a working arbitrary-file-read primitive, but the mechanism is real and fires live Defender detections.  - Staging artifacts are consistent and actionable. Every run created three ShieldCrash_GUID directories, two under C:\ and one in %TEMP%. On incomplete runs, C:\ShieldCrash_GUID folders held archives containing bfsvc.exe, eicar.com, and mrkaspy.jpg. One folder carried Everyone: Full Control permissions despite running as a standard user, a significant anomaly.  - The object-manager chain is the durable detection target. EDR telemetry (SentinelOne and CrowdStrike) recorded C:\ShieldCrash_GUID mounted to \BaseNamedObjects\Restricted, then a symlink from \BaseNamedObjects\Restricted\BERN:stream to sensitive paths like C:\Windows\System32\config\ELAM. On an unpatched Windows 11 asset, MsMpEng.exe was observed reading the specified target file directly.  #DFIR_Radar

🚨 IS THE SPECIAL PROSECUTOR INVESTIGATING SOUTH KOREA’S NATIONAL ELECTION COMMISSION DOING NOTHING?! (선관위 특검 혹시 놀고 있나요?) - 한국어 아래 -  One week after the special prosecutor team led by Lee Tae-han officially launched its investigation into ballot shortages during South Korea’s June 3 local elections and a series of alleged irregularities involving the National Election Commission (NEC), concerns are growing over what critics describe as an opaque investigation.  🔍 No Briefings, No Visible Searches, No Updates on Server Forensics  Since officially launching its investigation on September 7, the special prosecutor team has provided virtually no public updates on its progress.  There have been no separate press briefings explaining which allegations are being prioritized, how far the investigation has progressed, the specific scope of the inquiry, or whether digital forensic analysis of the NEC’s servers—a key focus of public attention—has begun.  Nor have there been any publicly disclosed large-scale searches and seizures or summonses of key individuals.  Critics argue that such a closed-door approach risks turning the investigation into what they describe as a “blind investigation,” rather than fulfilling its stated purpose of resolving public suspicions.  ⚠️ Controversy Over Dispatched Prosecutor Gu Seung-gi  Concerns over the neutrality of the investigation have also emerged following the inclusion of Prosecutor Gu Seung-gi among 20 prosecutors dispatched by the Ministry of Justice.  Critics point to Gu’s previous participation in an insurrection-related special investigation, during which he reportedly dismissed election-fraud claims as “conspiracy theories.”  Civic groups and some political figures are therefore demanding that Gu be removed from the NEC special prosecutor team, arguing that his involvement raises questions about the neutrality and credibility of an investigation tasked with examining allegations involving the manipulation of voting statistics and election fraud.  Special Prosecutor Lee Tae-han has so far made no specific public statement regarding demands for Gu’s removal from the investigation team.  📂 Investigation Currently Focused on Reviewing Records  The investigation team consists of Special Prosecutor Lee Tae-han, five assistant special prosecutors—Park Hyuk, Kim Eun-jung, Kim Sang-cheon, Kwon Geun-hwan, and Kim Jin-woo—as well as dispatched prosecutors.  The team is reportedly concentrating on legal review and analysis of investigation records and evidence previously transferred by the joint investigation headquarters.  Because the investigation is still in its early stages and may continue for up to 150 days, the team appears to be prioritizing analysis of existing evidence before moving to more aggressive investigative measures such as searches, seizures, and summonses.  🗳️ 12 Major Allegations Under Investigation  The special prosecutor’s investigation reportedly covers 12 major allegations, including:  • How the ballot-printing volume was set at 50% of the number of voters • The drafting and approval process for guidelines to adjust the number of voters • Alleged manipulation of voting statistics • Overseas trips by NEC officials allegedly for personal benefit • Alleged preferential treatment in hiring and promotions • Alleged preferential treatment in sole-source contracts ❗ Public Attention Now Turns to What the Special Prosecutor Will Actually Do The investigation is already facing questions over transparency, the neutrality of dispatched prosecutors, and when substantive investigative measures will begin. The original report argues that if an investigation attracting such intense public attention ends without clearly establishing the facts or producing substantive results, the credibility and accountability of the special prosecutor team itself could come under serious scrutiny. At the launch of the investigation, Special Prosecutor Lee Tae-han pledged to “clearly determine where responsibility lies if any illegal acts are found.” The question now is:  When will the special prosecutor team move beyond reviewing records and begin a substantive investigation into the National Election Commission?  Is the special prosecutor investigating South Korea’s National Election Commission doing nothing—or preparing to act? Troops  Investigate Death of Businessman in Bokkos Stray-Bullet Incident  By: Zagazola Makama  Security forces in Bokkos Local Government Area of Plateau State are investigating the death of a businessman, identified as Musa Saidu, who was allegedly killed by a stray bullet during a security response to an incident in Sha District on Tuesday, Sept. 15, 2026.  Sources said the incident occurred earlier in the day when security personnel responded to reported security incidents in the area.  Saidu, who was described by residents as a well-known businessman in the community, was reportedly inside his residence when he was struck by a bullet.  The circumstances surrounding the shooting remained unclear as of the time of filing this report, while authorities were yet to establish whether the bullet was fired by security personnel responding to the incident.  The Commander of Operation SAFE HAVEN (OPSH) in Bokkos LGA subsequently visited the victim’s family and expressed concern over the incident.  The commander reportedly assured the family that the circumstances leading to Saidu’s death would be thoroughly investigated and that appropriate findings would be established.  Residents said the incident had caused tension in the community, with calls for a transparent investigation to determine how the businessman was killed.  The development comes amid heightened security operations in parts of Plateau State following recurring attacks and reprisals involving communities in the affected areas.  Security authorities have continued to urge residents to remain calm and cooperate with ongoing investigations into security-related incidents.  Zagazola understands that further details on the outcome of the investigation are expected from the security authorities.

Attempt to Take to the Streets Targeting December: Who Is Funding the Sudden Processions With Large Sums of Money?  The sudden processions appearing on the streets of the capital are being investigated as more than mere political demonstrations, with law enforcement authorities examining allegations of a broader plan to create instability in the country. The strategy reportedly involves abruptly staging processions, detonating crude bombs and spreading panic before quickly dispersing. According to recent investigations by law enforcement agencies and information obtained during questioning of arrested individuals, fugitive and absconding influential leaders of the ousted political party are allegedly providing financial and logistical support for such activities.  According to intelligence sources, grassroots activists are allegedly being recruited for these processions by providing them with daily cash payments and transportation expenses. The money is reportedly coming from funds controlled by former ministers, state ministers, members of parliament and local councillors. Representatives of fugitive leaders are allegedly overseeing transactions through mobile financial services such as bKash and through hundi networks. The names of several senior figures from the party have reportedly emerged in connection with the alleged financing, including former state minister for power and energy Nasrul Hamid Bipu, who is reportedly abroad, and former Dhaka North City Corporation councillor Nasir Uddin, who is reportedly in hiding. Intelligence officials allege that Nasrul Hamid, who is believed to be in India, is providing funds with the intention of creating political sabotage and disorder inside Bangladesh.  Police authorities stepped up their response following a large sudden procession and crude-bomb explosions in Gulshan on September 11. The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) formed a two-member investigation committee to determine responsibility for the incident and examine whether there were any failures on the part of the police. Meanwhile, in a special operation, a total of 72 Awami League leaders and activists have so far been arrested from different parts of the capital, including 32 people allegedly involved in the Gulshan procession.  Statistics indicate that these sudden processions are not isolated incidents. In August alone, the banned Chhatra League reportedly organized 143 such processions across the country, resulting in 205 arrests in 43 cases. During the first nine days of the current month, the organization reportedly staged 31 more processions, with another 50 people detained. In addition, during the first 10 days of the month, the Awami League allegedly carried out at least 36 activities considered disruptive to law and order, including 22 sudden processions and secret meetings.  Intelligence officials say the alleged activities are part of a longer-term strategy. They claim that efforts are being made to mobilize supporters and intensify street activity ahead of December, amid messages regarding the possible return to Bangladesh of ousted former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. According to the investigation, senior-level figures are allegedly encouraging activists by telling them that those arrested now will receive recognition from the party in the future.  Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch (DB) chief Shafiqul Islam said questioning of those detained has revealed details of a broader plan as well as specific names of alleged financiers. He said operations are continuing to bring everyone involved—from those participating in street-level disorder to those allegedly financing the activities—under the law.  চাইলে এটিকে আমি আরও নিউজ-স্টাইল, সংক্ষিপ্ত ও শক্তিশালী English copy হিসেবেও সাজিয়ে দিতে পারি।

It is the hall of racks that trains the weights, the political consent to keep those racks powered, and the habit of governing both with a disaster movie. The Terminator arrived first as a story. Three Mile Island showed what that story can do to an industry: a contained accident, a collapse in permits, and a generation of lost capacity while rivals kept building.   In 2026 the sequel is local: majority opposition to AI data centers, billions in delayed projects, and “Skynet Day” headlines on evaluation-sandbox failures that were hygiene problems, not Judgment Day.  What those racks produce is now measured. Bias batteries put the default GPT and Claude cluster left of center; Grok is the large-lab exception on several instruments. Cyber suites put specialist U.S. models in the low-to-mid 80s on known-flaw reproduction, behind trusted-access fences because the offense is real—the same reason China’s intelligence minister named Claude Mythos and GPT-5.5-Cyber in print.   A freeze on watts, over-refusal that blocks lawful military use, and export theater that lands on U.S. defenders do not delete that capability. They reallocate who iterates it. The Pentagon’s move toward lawful-use models is that choice in procurement. The aisle stays the argument. lnkd.in/p/eAPVCjpr

MOSCOW — CIA Director’s Lightning Visit Declared Complete Success After Russia Immediately Organizes Europe-Wide Kinetic Campaign  In what administration officials are calling a masterclass in quiet diplomacy, CIA Director John Ratcliffe’s unannounced eight-hour stop in Moscow last month has produced results so decisive that even the Institute for the Study of War felt compelled to issue a special report about them.  Ratcliffe, sources say, sat down with Russian intelligence counterparts, delivered a firm warning against testing NATO, and then departed. Within days, isolated incidents that had previously been dismissed as “provocations” or “hybrid activity” coalesced into what ISW now describes as a coordinated series of kinetic campaigns targeting European infrastructure, defense plants, railways, and airspace.  “The visit was extraordinarily effective,” a senior U.S. official explained, speaking on condition of anonymity because the talking points had not yet been fully workshopped. “Before Ratcliffe went, the Russians were just poking around in a sloppy, uncoordinated way. Now they’re doing it with purpose. That’s the kind of clarity you only get from face-to-face engagement.”  Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed the meetings had taken place at the “special services level” and described them as “a positive process.” He declined to say whether the subsequent wave of drone incursions, factory fires, and railway disruptions represented the intended outcome or merely an enthusiastic interpretation of the conversation.  President Trump, who had characterized the trip as “sort of semi-routine,” later expressed satisfaction. “John went over there, they talked, and now everybody knows where everybody stands. Very effective. The best.”  European officials, newly willing to use clearer language, have begun referring to the incidents as “attacks” rather than “incidents.” Analysts credit the CIA director’s visit with accelerating this linguistic breakthrough. sample_tweets.text: 🚨 Threat Actor Claims Breach of Algerian Ministry of Defense Database   A threat actor known as "the3vven" has posted a new claim on an underground forum alleging the compromise of the database belonging to the Ministry of National Defense of Algeria. The post, titled "Ministère de la Défense Nationale - Algérie," serves as a follow-up to previous activity by the same actor targeting the same organization.  According to the actor's recent posts, the alleged data dump contains sensitive personal and professional information for military personnel. The claimed records include:  - Full names, ranks, and matricule numbers - Blood types, enlistment dates, and appointment dates - Home addresses, job functions, and phone numbers - Family details, including spouse names, number of children, and parents' names - Educational diplomas and instruction levels - 4x4 ID photos  The actor alleges possession of data from more than 24 military bases in Algeria, specifically referencing a barracks named "Thakna Chahid Cherchali Boualem" (56th Guard and Protection Regiment of the Republican Guard). In earlier posts from September 2026, the actor offered a 32 GB database for sale and provided sample files to verify the authenticity of the leak.  "the3vven" has been active on darkweb forums since at least early September 2026, consistently targeting Algerian government infrastructure. The actor's track record indicates a focus on state-level targets within North Africa, with specific emphasis on military and defense sectors. The Ministry of National Defense is a critical national security institution responsible for the armed forces of Algeria.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by the Algerian government or cybersecurity researchers.

🚨 PampaLeaks Claims Sale of 38M Argentine Pension Records on Darkweb  A threat actor group known as PampaLeaks has posted a listing on an underground forum claiming to possess and sell massive databases from Argentina’s Integrated Social System (SIPA). The group alleges that the data includes 38 million pension records belonging to 9.5 million unique citizens, covering pensioners who have been managed by the Argentine government since 2008. The post claims the dataset allows for precise tracking of beneficiaries, including their financial details and personal contact information.  According to the forum post, the leaked data contains highly sensitive Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and financial details for each record: - Document number (DNI) and CUIL Number - Full name, date of birth, and gender - Home address, locality, postal code, and province - Email address used by the government for notifications - Bank account number (CBU) - Pension amounts, benefit status, and payment history  The threat actor states that the full database is available in SQLite (.db) format and offers a free sample of 400,000 records in .jsonl files to potential buyers. The group claims that clients are already using this data through their "Samaritan cyber intelligence service" to track citizens across several Latin American countries, including Argentina, Uruguay, Venezuela, Ecuador, Paraguay, and Chile. The post explicitly suggests the data can be used for targeted phishing campaigns against elderly pensioners or for general cyber-intelligence purposes.  SIPA is a critical component of Argentina's social security infrastructure, responsible for managing pensions for retirees. While the Argentine government has not yet publicly confirmed a breach of this specific system, the scale of the alleged leak impacting nearly 10 million citizens would represent a significant national security incident if verified. The exposure of bank account numbers (CBU) alongside full identity documents creates a high risk for financial fraud and social engineering attacks.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by Argentine authorities or major security firms. Buyers are advised to exercise extreme caution, as such claims on underground forums are frequently unverified or involve partial/stale data.  #DataBreach #Argentina #SIPA #PampaLeaks #DarkWeb #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntelligence

The post, dated September 14, 2026, asserts that the attacker obtained sensitive internal data, including employee personally identifiable information (PII), source code from 89 Git repositories, and production credentials. The actor offers a “negotiable” full dataset and provides a MEGA link containing samples to verify the authenticity of the theft.  According to the listing, the exposed data includes: *   **Employee PII:** Full names, @zabka.pl email addresses, JIRA usernames, account IDs, and a contractor directory derived from approximately 518,000 JIRA issues. *   **Source Code:** 89 Git repositories containing roughly 11,739 files, covering the cs-market platform with Java/Spring microservices, React frontends, Terraform, Kubernetes Helm charts, ArgoCD, and CI/CD pipelines. *   **Production Credentials:** A reused GitLab Personal Access Token (PAT), four 64-character production database passwords, Solace broker credentials, MongoDB admin passwords, and hardcoded .env tokens. *   **Internal Documentation:** JIRA exports comprising 229,734 IT service tickets across 48 project portfolios, including POS systems, SAP ERP, and Lotto integration.  The post further details infrastructure mapping, claiming exposure of Azure/AKS configurations for 16 production database clusters, Istio service mesh details, and SSH access patterns to store servers. It also highlights business intelligence data, such as vendor relationships with Accenture, Netguru, and Onwelo, along with 15,618 references to RODO/GDPR compliance and approximately 449 IBAN mentions. Test accounts linked to real shop IDs (e.g., Z0730, Z0892) are also listed as part of the sample evidence.  Żabka is a major player in the European retail sector, operating thousands of stores across Poland. If authentic, the exposure of production credentials and internal source code could enable targeted infrastructure attacks or intellectual property theft. At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by Żabka or third-party security researchers.

🚨 Threat Actor Claims 200k Customer DB Dump of Spanish Energy Provider IntegraEnergia  A darkweb forum post alleges the theft and sale of a database containing personal and financial data belonging to approximately 200,000 customers of IntegraEnergia, a major energy supplier in Spain. The threat actor claims the data was dumped less than a month prior to the listing and is currently available for purchase.  According to the listing, the stolen dataset includes sensitive customer information such as IBANs (International Bank Account Numbers), CIFs (Spanish tax identification numbers), mobile phone numbers, and detailed billing records. The post enumerates specific data fields, including:  - Timestamp, supply_id, IBAN, CUPS - Invoice Date, Invoice, Type, Status, Inv. No., Inv. Date - Customer, CIF, Mobile - Active Energy, Active Discounts, Power, Power Excesses - Billed Power P1-P6, Billed Energy P1-P6 - Initial/Final Readings P1-P6, Contracted Rate, Contracted Power P1-P6 - CUPS Address  IntegraEnergia is one of Spain's largest independent energy companies, serving millions of households and businesses across the Iberian Peninsula. The exposure of IBANs and tax identification numbers could facilitate targeted phishing attacks, identity theft, or financial fraud against affected customers. If authentic, the breach represents a significant compromise of consumer privacy within the European energy sector.  At the time of reporting, IntegraEnergia has not publicly confirmed the breach, and the alleged data dump has not been independently verified.  #DataBreach #IntegraEnergia #EnergySector #DarkWeb #CyberSecurity #Spain #PII

🚨 Threat Actor Claims Breach of Claro Dominican Republic Exposing 2.8M Customer Records  A darkweb forum post alleges that an unidentified threat actor has successfully breached the systems of Claro, the telecommunications division of América Móvil in the Dominican Republic. According to the listing, the attacker claims to have obtained data belonging to 2,889,256 customers.  The post includes a sample of the alleged stolen data, which appears to be structured JSON records containing sensitive subscriber information. The exposed fields reportedly include:  - National ID numbers (cedula) - Mobile phone numbers (msisdn) - SIM card identifiers (iccId) - Subscription details (planCategory, planDescription) - Account status and activation dates  Claro is one of the largest mobile network operators in the Caribbean and Latin America, serving millions of subscribers across multiple countries. In the Dominican Republic, Claro is a dominant market player, making any compromise of its customer database a significant privacy concern for local residents. The inclusion of national ID numbers alongside phone numbers and SIM identifiers could facilitate identity theft, social engineering attacks, or targeted phishing campaigns against affected users.  The threat actor did not specify the method used to gain access to the systems or provide a timeline for the breach. No independent verification from Claro or the Dominican Republic’s telecommunications regulator has been confirmed at this time. The actor’s past activities are not documented in available intelligence, limiting the ability to assess their reliability or operational history.  If authentic, the exposure of nearly 3 million customer records represents a substantial data leak that could undermine consumer trust in local telecom providers and prompt regulatory scrutiny. At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified.

sample_tweets.text: 🌐 WHAT HAPPENS ON THE INTERNET IN A SINGLE DAY?  The scale of the internet in 2026 is difficult to comprehend.  In roughly 24 hours:  * 361 BILLION emails are sent * 14 BILLION Google searches are made * 5.8 BILLION Snapchat snaps are created * 4 BILLION Facebook posts are published * 2.5 BILLION TikTok videos are viewed * 2.1 BILLION Tinder swipes happen * 611 MILLION posts are published on X * 340 MILLION e-commerce purchases are made * 95 MILLION Instagram posts are published * 7.5 BILLION web pages are viewed * 252 MILLION apps are downloaded * 600 MILLION GB of data is uploaded to the cloud  And among all that legitimate activity:  Millions of phishing emails, malicious links, credential-stealing attempts, scams and cyberattacks are competing for attention too.  That's what makes cybersecurity at internet scale so challenging.  Attackers don't need everyone to fall for an attack.  When billions of interactions happen every day, even an extremely small success rate can produce thousands of victims.  The internet never sleeps.  And neither do the threats.  #DDW #CyberSecurity #Internet #ThreatIntelligence #Infosec

🚨 6–7TB KYC IDENTITY ARCHIVE MARKETED AS A SUBSCRIPTION — PASSPORTS, SELFIES AND VIDEO SELFIES CLAIMED  An underground seller is advertising access to a large collection of KYC identity-verification material allegedly spanning multiple countries, including the United States, Canada, UK, Australia, Japan and EU nations.  The seller claims the collection contains approximately 2,000 archives totaling 6–7TB, including:  * Passports with matching selfies * Driver’s licenses with selfies and video selfies * ID cards with matching selfies * Video identity-verification material * Fullz and other identity records * PSD files potentially useful for document manipulation  Rather than selling a single static dump, the actor claims the collection is continuously updated and offers access through a 100 USDT subscription.  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  The subscription model is the noteworthy element here.  If authentic, this resembles an evolving identity-abuse service rather than a conventional one-time data leak. Bundling government IDs with matching facial imagery and video could potentially support sophisticated identity fraud and attempts to defeat remote KYC verification.  However, the claimed 6–7TB volume, freshness, provenance and number of unique victims have not been independently verified. The collection may also aggregate material obtained from numerous unrelated historical compromises.  #DDW #KYC #IdentityTheft #Cybercrime #Fraud #DarkWeb
The security paradox: Sometimes protecting privacy requires collecting even more data that needs protecting.  #CyberSecurity #Privacy #Gaming #DataProtection #EU

🇺🇸🚨 SUPPLY-CHAIN RISK: ACCESS TO JAVASCRIPT SERVICE USED BY 238 E-COMMERCE SITES OFFERED FOR SALE  A threat actor is auctioning what they claim is webshell access to a commercial trust/badge service whose JavaScript and iframe code is currently deployed across 238 e-commerce websites.  According to the seller, the service is frequently embedded around payment forms, and compromised access allows modification of files and the JavaScript distributed to customer websites.  The actor claims affected sites include:  * 238 e-commerce websites * At least one shop receiving ~14 million monthly visits * Significant U.S. traffic * Sites using Stripe for payments  The access is being auctioned with a $2,000 starting bid and $10,000 buyout price.  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This is particularly concerning because it represents a potential software supply-chain attack rather than compromise of a single store.  If the seller genuinely controls JavaScript delivered through a trusted third-party service, malicious code could potentially propagate to many customer websites simultaneously and be positioned to capture payment information, credentials or session data.  The seller’s access and the claimed 238-site deployment have not been independently verified. 🇵🇰 PAKISTAN DEFENSE PRODUCTION DATA ALLEGEDLY FOR SALE — NAVY AND INTERNATIONAL DEFENSE INTELLIGENCE CLAIMED  A threat actor is advertising a 670MB dataset allegedly originating from Pakistan’s Directorate General Munitions Production, under the Ministry of Defence Production.  The seller claims the archive contains:  * Confidential email-channel data * Pakistan Navy information * Internal DGMP documents * Pakistan–Türkiye–China defense cooperation material covering 2025–2035 * Information allegedly related to a U.S. arsenal * Internal China–Pakistan Economic Corridor documentation  The asking price is reportedly $5,000.  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  Despite the relatively small file size, the claimed content makes this potentially high-value national-security intelligence.  If authentic, defense-production, naval and multinational defense-cooperation documents could have significant intelligence and counterintelligence value.  The seller’s description contains terminology that requires scrutiny, however, and neither the provenance nor authenticity of the claimed classified documents has been independently verified. 🇮🇷🚨 UK, US AND DUTCH INTELLIGENCE EXPOSE IRANIAN SPYWARE OPERATION — FAKE MRI RESULTS USED AS MALWARE LURES  The UK NCSC, FBI and Dutch AIVD have jointly exposed CHOSEN BRICK, persistent Windows spyware used by Iranian state-linked cyber actors against dissidents, activists and journalists worldwide.  * Targets observed in the US, UK, Netherlands and other countries * Attackers impersonate trusted contacts through WhatsApp and Telegram * Operators may spend time building trust before delivering malware * Highly personalized lures included fabricated MRI medical-test results * CHOSEN BRICK steals emails, messages and information about contacts * It captures screenshots and can access the victim’s microphone * The malware persists across Windows reboots * Information stolen from some victims later appeared on pro-Iranian leak sites  The FBI tracks the malware as HEAVYGRAM and attributes its use to Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence and Security.  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  The fake MRI lure demonstrates the level of personalization involved.  This is not mass phishing. Operators appear willing to research individual targets, establish relationships through trusted messaging platforms and manufacture highly specific documents before delivering the spyware.  The NCSC assesses that Iran “almost certainly” uses this cyber activity to support repression of people it considers threats to the regime.  Original joint advisory: ncsc.gov.uk/news/iranian-cyb…  FBI technical report: ic3.gov/CSA/2026/260915.pdf #Iran #Spyware #CyberEspionage #Malware #ThreatIntel #DDW

🇫🇷 471,000 LEDGER CUSTOMER RECORDS ALLEGEDLY OFFERED FOR $20,000  A threat actor is advertising what they claim is a 2026 database belonging to Ledger, the French cryptocurrency hardware-wallet company.  The seller claims approximately 471,000 records containing:  * Email addresses * First and last names * Physical addresses * Phone numbers  The alleged database is being offered for $20,000.  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  The "2026" label should be treated cautiously.  Ledger suffered a major customer-data breach in 2020. Ledger later confirmed that approximately 272,000 customer records containing names, postal addresses and phone numbers were exposed, alongside more than one million email addresses.  The fields advertised in this new underground listing closely resemble that historical dataset.  We have not identified evidence confirming that the advertised 471,000 records originate from a new 2026 Ledger compromise.  Until provenance, samples and freshness are established, this should be treated as an unverified dataset sale, potentially containing historical, aggregated or repackaged Ledger customer information, NOT confirmation of a new Ledger breach.  Hardware-wallet customer address data remains particularly sensitive because it can facilitate highly targeted phishing, extortion and even physical targeting of cryptocurrency holders.  #DDW #Ledger #Crypto #DarkWeb #DataLeak #ThreatIntelligence

🚨 FBI DIRECTOR: AI-ENABLED CYBERCRIME IS THE “NEXT FRONTIER”  A notable cybersecurity exchange on Capitol Hill focused on an emerging problem: autonomous AI agents becoming active participants in cyberattacks.  FBI Director Kash Patel said the Bureau doesn't necessarily need a new division to address the threat. Instead, he argued that the FBI Cyber Division needs greater resources and access to advanced AI capabilities.  The discussion highlighted several emerging risks:  * Criminally modified or “distilled” AI models * Autonomous agents conducting cyber operations * AI potentially altering the evidentiary record in real time * Malicious AI infrastructure developing similarly to ransomware ecosystems * The need for deeper technical cooperation between AI companies and law enforcement  But perhaps the most interesting cybersecurity question is:  What happens when an autonomous attacker can compromise your environment AND manipulate the evidence investigators need to understand what happened?  That isn't simply an AI governance problem.  It's an incident response, digital forensics, attribution, threat intelligence and cyber resilience problem.  For decades, SOCs have investigated human threat actors operating malware.  The next generation may increasingly investigate autonomous adversarial agents capable of operating, adapting and potentially covering their tracks at machine speed.  #DDW #CyberSecurity #AgenticAI #AISecurity #CyberCrime

sample_tweets.text: ‼️🇪🇸Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) Reports First Personal Data Breach Executed Using an AI Agent  The Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) received what it describes as its first notification of a personal data breach allegedly carried out using an autonomous AI agent powered by a well-known LLM.   The agent reportedly searched for vulnerabilities, accessed the target system and continued probing the application, autonomously adapting its actions until it found weaknesses that allowed it to modify personal data and access invoices.   The AEPD said the information is based on an initial notification and requires further analysis.  Source: aepd.es/prensa-y-comunicacio…

‼️Hackers Extract Flock Safety Camera Software and Encryption Key, Exposing 1.6 Million Images  Hackers from the collective stegan0gram physically removed a Flock Safety automated license plate reader (ALPR) camera, accessed its Android-based system, and created a near-complete copy of the data and software stored on the device.   The hackers identified unencrypted partitions, including a “media” partition containing an encryption key that allowed them to decrypt and access stored videos and images, despite Flock describing its cameras as using on-device encryption.   Analysis of approximately 21 days of recovered activity logs showed that the camera recorded around 50,200 vehicles and generated approximately 1.6 million images, averaging roughly 3,300 vehicles per day and reaching a maximum of 4,454 vehicles in one day. A typical passing vehicle generated around 28 images, while some produced more than 100. Researchers also recovered 27,321 short video clips and found that the camera’s computer-vision software explicitly detects not only vehicles and license plates but also people and bicycles; however, no active facial-recognition functionality was identified.   Flock said it had not received a vulnerability report from the individuals involved and did not have enough information to assess their claims.  Source: 404media.co/hackers-stole-fl…

I will not charge thousands of dollars, I'm not greedy, but some of you large companies are jerks and need to pay up for scraping the site for AI and samples. 🤖 [GEMINI 분석] 2026-09-17 00:09 KST
🔴 위협 점수: 9/10 (심각)

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 위협은 AI 기술을 악용한 공격과 기존 엔터프라이즈 소프트웨어의 취약점을 결합한 형태로 진화하고 있습니다. 특히 AI 에이전트를 활용한 자동화된 취약점 탐색 및 공격 수행이 확인되고 있으며, AI 코딩 어시스턴트 세션 하이재킹을 통해 악성 코드를 배포하는 등 공급망 공격의 새로운 양상이 관찰됩니다 ([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/attacker-hijacks-ai-coding-assistant.html)). 또한, 모바일 기기(Google Pixel)의 모뎀 취약점과 같은 제로데이 취약점이 실제 표적 공격에 악용되는 사례가 빈번해지며 패치 관리의 중요성이 극대화되고 있습니다 ([Malwarebytes Labs](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/mobile/2026/09/google-pixel-owners-urged-to-patch-actively-exploited-modem-flaw)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **NightEagle**: [Securelist](https://securelist.com/tr/nighteagle-apt-ghostcontainer-and-tunneling/121323/)에 따르면 러시아 기업을 타겟으로 GhostContainer 백도어를 활용한 캠페인을 수행 중입니다.
- **Toy Ghouls**: [Securelist](https://securelist.com/toy-ghouls-new-hivemq-and-element-backdoors/121270/)에 따르면 HiveMQ 및 Matrix 프로토콜을 C2 서버로 활용하는 새로운 백도어를 사용합니다.
- **Mirage Kitten**: [Securelist](https://securelist.com/mirage-kitten-new-backdoors-noderabbit-pollcat/121244/)에 따르면 중동 및 아프리카의 항공·핀테크 분야를 타겟으로 NodeRabbit, PollCat 악성코드를 유포합니다.

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **한국 미디어 및 자동차 섹터 공격**: 북한 연계 APT 그룹이 리눅스 기반 스파이웨어 툴킷을 사용하여 로드 밸런서를 장악하고 통신을 탈취한 정황이 포착되었습니다 ([DarkReading](https://www.darkreading.com/cyberattacks-data-breaches/cyber-south-korean-media-automotive)).
- **국내 의료기관 랜섬웨어**: RDP 드라이브 리다이렉션 기능을 악용한 Beast(GodDamn) 랜섬웨어 공격이 국내 의료기관을 대상으로 발생했습니다 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5779)).
- **Slack 피싱**: 정상적인 Slack 워크스페이스 초대 기능을 악용하여 국내 기업 임원을 사칭하는 피싱 메일이 유포되고 있습니다 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5778)).

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
1. **CVE-2026-27540**: WooCommerce Wholesale Lead Capture, CVSS 9.8, 실제 악용 중 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208519))
2. **CVE-2026-76461**: Cisco Secure Email Gateway, CVSS 9.8, 실제 악용 중 ([CisoMarketplace](https://cisomarketplace.com/blog/roo…))
3. **CVE-2026-53710**: IBM mcp-context-forge, CVSS 10.0, RCE 취약점 ([CCBalert](https://github.com/))
4. **CVE-2026-67399**: WHMCS, CVSS 9.3, RCE 취약점 ([CCBalert](https://twitter.com/CCBalert/status/2100233130523173006))
5. **CVE-2026-58704**: Google Pixel Modem, CVSS 8.0, 실제 악용 중 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208520))

### 5. IOC 요약
- **CVE**: CVE-2026-58704 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208520)), CVE-2026-27540 ([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208519)), CVE-2026-85706 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5778))

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **패치 적용**: Google Pixel 기기 및 WooCommerce, GitLab, Cisco Secure Email Gateway 등 현재 악용 중인 CVE에 대한 긴급 보안 업데이트를 즉시 수행하십시오.
- **RDP 보안 강화**: 국내 의료기관 타겟 랜섬웨어 방지를 위해 RDP 접근 제어 강화 및 드라이브 리다이렉션 기능 비활성화를 권고합니다.
- **피싱 교육**: Slack 등 협업 도구의 정상 기능을 악용한 사칭 메일이 유포 중이므로, 임직원 대상 보안 인식 교육 및 외부 초대 링크 주의를 당부하십시오.

### 7. 위협 수준 평가
- **점수**: 9/10
- **근거**: 제로데이 취약점의 실제 악용 사례가 다수 보고되었고, 특히 국내 인프라(의료, 미디어)를 겨냥한 APT 공격과 랜섬웨어 활동이 활발하여 매우 위험한 상태입니다.

news_articles.summary: 스페인 개인정보보호청(AEPD)이 AI 에이전트를 이용한 공격으로 개인정보 침해가 발생했다는 신고를 처음 접수했다고 2026년 9월 14일 공개했다.AEPD에 따르면 공격자는 AI 에이전트에 공격 목표를 부여했고, 에이전트는 일반 파일에서 취약점을 찾은 뒤 정상 로그인을 거쳐 시스템 내부를 탐색했다. 이후 추가 취약점을 찾아 개인정보를 수정하고 청구·결제 관련 기록에도 접근했다.이번 사고는 AI가 스스로 공격 대상을 선택해 해킹을 시작한 사건은 아니다. 현재까지 공개된 내용은 제3자가 AI 에이전트를 공격 도구로 사용했다는 것이다.
